text:
rui_chen: Quick note from model bring-up: Asteria-v2 fp16 vs q4x. Baseline looks fine but q4x detok shows emoji/ZWJ clusters and mixed numerals splitting unexpectedly in vertical subtitle samples.

sofia_g: can you paste the minimal repro sample?

rui_chen: repro (vertical-like input with ruby/brackets + ZWJ emoji + Arabic-Indic digits):
```
彼

(Example shortened)
59
59
59
59
```
(OK, above has vertical markers removed in paste. Real input: "太郎《たろう》は656667\u200d4693fb3fbに向かった。")

dmitri_v: ugh the paste mangled, but got it from your artifact. expected detok: "太郎《たろう》は\u0665\u0666\u0667\u200d👩🏻‍👩🏻に向かった。"
q4x output (detok): "太郎《たろう》は 6 67 👩 🏻 ‍  👩 🏻 に向かった。"

brad_s: so Arabic-Indic cluster \u0665\u0666\u0667 collapsed to "6 67" (latin 6 then 67) and the emoji ZWJ family got split across multiple tokens, losing the joined glyph. That's a pretty visible regression.

sofia_g: did you verify tokenizer/version parity? packaging differences again?

rui_chen: tokenizer hash matches across builds. But the q4x packaging step runs a post-process that prunes "rare multi-codepoint tokens" to reduce vocab size for quant runtime. packaging log shows "INFO: pruned multi-codepoint tokens: 123 entries" and a line listing some example ranges including ZWJ and Arabic-Indic clusters.

dmitri_v: that pruning sounds like a no-no for multilocale. Why would pack step remove tokens rather than remap?

rui_chen: it's an internal opt: we thought long multi-codepoint tokens rarely used and hurt memory. clearly for languages with ZWJ emoji and vertical subtitle rubies this is harmful.

brad_s: can you show tokenized sequences?

rui_chen: tokenized fp16 (ids replaced with readable pieces):
[ 太郎, 《, たろう, 》, は, \u0665\u0666\u0667, \u200d👩🏻‍👩🏻, に, 向かった, 。 ]
q4x tokenized:
[ 太郎, 《, たろう, 》, は, 6, 67, \u200d👩, 🏻, \r, 👩, 🏻, に, 向かった, 。 ]

sofia_g: that matches detok. Two separate issues: (1) numeral cluster replaced by latin fallback (maybe canonicalization during pack?), (2) ZWJ family token split. Both likely from pruning + a normalization map applied at pack-time to reduce token granularity.

dmitri_v: we need a short-term mitigation and a long-term policy. Short-term: abort q4x rollout and revert to fp16 in prod. Long-term: remove pruning or restrict to ascii-only merges, add unit tests covering emoji ZWJ sequences and Arabic-Indic ranges. Also check any normalized-to-latin mappings.

sofia_g: who owns the rollback? I'll touch the release gating doc and block q4x until we fix pack logic. @brad_s can you open a triage ticket and attach the failing sample and packaging log?

brad_s: opened ML-5299 (Asteria-v2 q4x token-prune regression) and uploaded artifacts + packaging logs + smoketest diff: https://redwood.test/triage/ML-5299. evals-bot also posted a regression alert: multilocale/emoji-zwj BLEU -4.8 (q4x vs fp16) and tokenization drift metric +14.1% (https://redwood.test/evals/1767401234).

rui_chen: I've already rebuilt a q4x artifact with pruning disabled and ran a quick smoke: matches fp16 detok. pushing that build to staging for runtime QA.

dmitri_v: follow-up items: 1) add token-coverage check in pack-artifact to ensure number of tokens covering codepoint classes (emoji ZWJ families, Arabic-Indic, fullwidth digits, ruby brackets) doesn't drop below 99.9% of baseline; 2) add an eval smoke (vertical subtitle + family emoji) in nightly; 3) re-run the whole multilocale suite before unblocking q4x rollout.

sofia_g: i'll draft the PRs for 1) and 2). brad, assign ML-5299 to me and dmitri for ownership.

brad_s: assigned. rolling back q4x in prod pools now, tagging eng-runtime.

evals-bot: Regression triage ML-5299 created and linked to eval run 1767401234.

sofia_g: thanks everyone. small ask: can pack-artifact emit a human readable "token-prune-candidates" file during build so we can audit before release? that would have caught this quickly.

rui_chen: good idea. adding to follow-up. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
